title: Make the zoned date helpers correct across daylight-saving changes
summary: An existing time-zone helper library gives wrong results on days when clocks change. CI has 3 failing tests. The library must become correct; the existing tests describe the intended behavior.
users: The scheduling app that books appointments in its customers' local time.
nonGoals: New functions beyond the five listed
Calendars other than the Gregorian calendar
interface:
Existing `src/zoned.ts` exports, keep the signatures: `offsetAt(instant, tz)`, `localDate(instant, tz)`, `formatLocal(instant, tz)`, `startOfDay(instant, tz)`, `addDays(instant, days, tz)`. Node.js 24 built-ins only (Intl is available); erasable TypeScript only.

Rules for converting a local wall-clock time back to an instant:
- If the local time does not exist (the clocks jumped forward over it), use the instant obtained with the offset in force **before** the jump. For example, 02:30 on 2026-03-08 in New York becomes 03:30 EDT.
- If the local time happens twice (the clocks went back), use the **earlier** instant.

The existing tests in `tests/zoned.test.ts` describe the required behavior. They must all pass, unchanged.

stories.title: Same time on the next day
stories.iWant: "same time tomorrow" to keep the local clock time even when clocks change
stories.soThat: appointments do not move by an hour
stories.gherkin:
Scenario: spring change
  Given 2026-03-07 09:00 in America/New_York
  When I add 1 day
  Then the local time is 2026-03-08 09:00

Scenario: missing local time
  Given 2026-03-07 02:30 in America/New_York
  When I add 1 day
  Then the local time is 2026-03-08 03:30

stories.title: Start of the local day
stories.iWant: the exact instant a local day starts
stories.soThat: daily reports cover the right hours
stories.gherkin:
Scenario: day of change
  Given 2026-03-08 15:00 in America/New_York
  When I ask for the start of that day
  Then the result is 2026-03-08T05:00:00Z

frs.title: addDays keeps wall-clock time
frs.text: When addDays is called, the system shall return the instant with the same local wall-clock time `days` calendar days later in the zone, applying the gap and overlap rules when that local time does not exist or happens twice.

frs.title: startOfDay is local midnight
frs.text: When startOfDay is called, the system shall return the instant of the first moment of the local calendar day containing `instant`, using the offset in force at that moment.

frs.title: Existing behavior kept
frs.text: The system shall keep offsetAt, localDate and formatLocal correct, and all existing tests shall pass without being changed, skipped or weakened.

nfrs.title: No dependencies
nfrs.text: The library shall use only Node.js built-ins.
